author: Tynvale
body:
Just showcasing some ideas that I think can improve the staff, forums and in-game!

Forum Ideas

Threads allowing iframe

As most of you may know, I do Youtube and post my videos on the forums. In one of my classes at school I learn a little bit of code, and I came up with what I think is a great idea for the forums. I was messing around a little bit and came up with this:

This coding was working until I posted the thread, so my idea was to make the forums able to hold this type of coding since it would help out a lot with video posting on the forums and looks much more professional. To stop people abusing it and putting inappropriate links, if it's possible maybe only allow YouTube videos; or the staff can handle it.


Direct Messaging on the forums

This could work like something similar to sites like Twitter, Facebook and even Youtube. You could go onto the person profile, click on a button that sends a message. Then that message can be seen by the receiver in their alerts. This would make communication for things such as scrims and private conversations much easier. It would also benefit people who may not have Skype, Slack or anything else that is typically used for communication.


Idea Section on the forums

I know that 'Server Feedback' is where people put their ideas at the moment; I think that making an actual section for suggestions would become much more organised. Server Feedback to me sounds like the purpose of it is to give general feedback/opinions on how the server is running, it doesn't really suggest anywhere that a suggestion can be put there and making a separate tab would help point out to new forum users that's where to go for ideas. Maybe to get more people on the forums and to gather more suggestions, link the section in-game.


Staff System Ideas

Improved work/effeciency

During the explanation I am going to refer to real life scenarios to hopefully make it easier to understand. I wanted to try to think of a new system because as a lot of people know the staff are going quite fast, and whether it's a demotion or someone retiring it doesn't really matter. I personally think that some new system needs to be implemented and even trialed to help improve the staff as a whole. So here's the idea...

Lets say that Avicus is a business, these would be the roles:
- Admins would be Managers
- Sr Mods would be the Experienced Workers
- Mods would be the majority of the workplace as Workers
- Players would be the customers

If someone were to run this business they would need to assign certain roles to certain workers. But on Avicus it seems like it's the opposite, from what I have seen and experienced the staff hardly get any training and don't get told specific roles to that certain person. They are just expected to know and do what is set. And just like a business if you don't do it up to standards you will be fired/demoted. This is fine and all but you will eventually run into problems like the ones we a currently having.

One way I think it could be fixed is by opening up spots for certain roles. these roles could be things such as:
- Community Manager (talk regularly to community and make sure that there suggestions are being heard)
- Social Manager (organise and control the Avicus social media pages)
- Communications Manager (regular update everyone on things being planned/organised)
And many others roles...

These roles could be applied for just like Mod applications by members of the community and even existing mods. I think that if this was to be implemented it would have to be up to the existing staff to decide if that is your main role or if it is extra work from being a regular staff member. No matter their decision on the roles, every staff member needs professionally treated training.

Some pros of this system are:
- Everything will look much more professional and organised
- Mods won't "compete" against eachother and they will have their own little jobs.
- Allows the work flow and communication of staff to improve
- Involves the community more with roles such as a Community Manager 

Some cons of this system are:
- Will probably need 1-3 people on one role because of timezone issues
- Might end up having lots of staff because of so many different roles, causing the server to have way too much staff

To some it all up basically give a staff member a certain job, as well as general moderating. So if a part of the staff is slacking you can see who it is and deal with it accordingly.


In-game Ideas

More reasons to gain credits

At the moment, the only main goal of getting credits is to get a cool badge, there is other stuff available but they don't seem to give as much reward as a new badge would. I was thinking that in the hub we could have a 'casino' section where you can risk your credits. It would be quite interesting to have jackpots as things such as a gold rank for a week or 50k credits; because the higher the rewards, the more the player has to gain credits. Therefore gaining the player more playtime and they may even buy a rank to help them in the credits they are trying to obtain. All this seems like quite great benefits for the server


More reasons to have a rank

The only thing really useful now with a rank is the credit boost. We need to have much more for offer if we want to continue having people buy ranks. There isn't much else to say, other than it should give the user a 'slight' advantage over a non-donor since they have supported the server and actually paid money for it. Maybe when the player count goes back up and there are more donors, a rotation that only donors could play may be an option...


Bring back the shop in-game

Enough said...


So there we go; these are just some suggestion I have. I have suggested some of these and there may be that have been thought of by others in the past but they are ideas that I think can improve the server greatly and I wanted it all in one place, what do you think?
